f: Dennis Brown began recording when he was just eleven years old and went on to make more than 75 albums.
Bob Marley called Dennis Brown his favourite singer, and the nickname stuck: the Crown Prince of Reggae.
Gregory Isaacs' smooth, aching voice earned him the nickname the Cool Ruler.
His 1982 album Night Nurse, with Sly and Robbie on rhythm, is the record most people know him by.
Horace Andy sang on Massive Attack's "Angel", which brought his trembling falsetto to a whole new audience.
"Skylarking" is the Horace Andy song that roots reggae fans still treasure.
Burning Spear is the stage name of Winston Rodney, one of the most influential roots reggae artists of the 1970s.
Winston Rodney took his stage name from a nickname of Kenya's first president, Jomo Kenyatta.
Max Romeo's 1968 song "Wet Dream" climbed the UK charts even though radio refused to play it.
In 1976 Max Romeo made War ina Babylon with Lee "Scratch" Perry, one of roots reggae's classic albums.
Prince Buster, born Cecil Campbell, made records in the 1960s that shaped ska and rocksteady.
The British band Madness took their name from a Prince Buster song.
Lee "Scratch" Perry built his own studio, the Black Ark, behind his house in Kingston and made landmark dub and reggae records there.
Perry's Black Ark studio burned down in 1979.
The Heptones' three-part harmonies helped carry Jamaican music from ska and rocksteady into reggae.
Heptones lead singer Leroy Sibbles also played bass at Studio One, and his basslines are still reused today.
The Wailing Souls go back to the 1960s, and Winston "Pipe" Matthews and Lloyd "Bread" McDonald were the two constant members.
The Wailing Souls were nominated for Grammy Awards three times.
Black Uhuru's album Anthem won the first ever Grammy for Best Reggae Album, in 1985.
Black Uhuru started in 1972 as Uhuru, and Duckie Simpson was the one member who stayed throughout.
Junior Murvin's "Police and Thieves" was produced by Lee "Scratch" Perry in 1976 and was later covered by The Clash.
Junior Reid sang lead for Black Uhuru from 1986 to 1988.
Junior Reid is also known for a guest appearance on The Game's 2006 single "It's Okay".
Eek-A-Mouse, real name Ripton Hylton, was one of the first singjays, mixing singing and deejaying with his own style of scatting.
Eek-A-Mouse is known for flashy, eccentric costumes on stage.
Barrington Levy comes from Clarendon, Jamaica, and was one of the key voices of early-1980s dancehall.
Freddie McGregor started his music career when he was only seven years old.
Freddie McGregor is a producer as well as a singer.
Johnny Osbourne's album Truths and Rights was a roots reggae success, and its title track and "Jah Promise" are the highlights.
Don Carlos was an early member of Black Uhuru before he went solo.
Michael Rose was the lead voice of Black Uhuru during their 1980s peak, including the Grammy-winning album Anthem.
Pablo Moses' 1975 debut album Revolutionary Dream is a roots reggae favourite.
Don Drummond was a trombonist and composer, an original member of The Skatalites who wrote many of their tunes.
The Skatalites backed Bob Marley and The Wailers on their first single, "Simmer Down".
The Skatalites' best-known tunes include "Guns of Navarone", and they reformed in 1983 and have played together ever since.
Alton Ellis is known as the Godfather of Rocksteady.
Alton Ellis' younger sister, Hortense Ellis, was a reggae singer too.
The Paragons' "The Tide Is High" was written by group member John Holt and became a worldwide hit for Blondie in 1980.
Bob Andy, born Keith Anderson, is widely regarded as one of reggae's most influential songwriters.
Bob Andy and Marcia Griffiths had a UK hit in 1970 with "Young, Gifted and Black".
Marcia Griffiths is called the Queen of Reggae, and her 1989 remix of "Electric Boogie" gave the Electric Slide dance its music.
Junior Delgado, born Oscar Hibbert, was famed for his roots reggae style.
Johnny Clarke is best known for his recordings with producer Bunny Lee in the 1970s.
Errol Dunkley was born in Kingston, and his song "OK Fred" was a UK hit in 1979.
Freddie McKay's career ran from the rocksteady era into spiritual roots reggae.
Cornell Campbell, also called Don Gorgon, is known for his trademark falsetto.
Cornell Campbell made his name at Studio One in the late 1960s, then worked with producer Bunny Lee in the 1970s.
Al Campbell has been singing since the late 1960s.
Bim Sherman was born Jarret Vincent in Jamaica, and later recorded with Adrian Sherwood's On-U Sound label in England.
The Mighty Diamonds formed in 1969, and their 1976 debut album Right Time is a roots reggae classic.
Leroy Smart is a singer, songwriter and producer from Kingston, Jamaica.
Echo Minott's breakthrough hit was "Lazy Body" in 1985.
Little Roy recorded a reggae version of Nirvana songs, released as Battle for Seattle in 2010.
Peter Broggs, born Henry James, was a roots reggae singer and songwriter.
Winston McAnuff, also known as Electric Dread, is a Jamaican singer and composer of reggae and dub.
Carlton Livingston is known for his 1984 hit "100 Weight of Collie Weed".
Linval Thompson is a roots reggae singer, dub musician and record producer.
Hopeton Lewis was a rocksteady and reggae singer and arranger, and his song "Take It Easy" is often called the first rocksteady record.
Hortense Ellis was the younger sister of the singer Alton Ellis.
Winston Francis, known as Mr Fix It, began his singing career in the 1960s.
Bob Marley was born in Nine Mile, Saint Ann, Jamaica, in 1945.
The Skatalites played on The Wailers' first single, "Simmer Down", back in 1964.
Time magazine named Bob Marley and the Wailers' Exodus the best album of the 20th century.
Peter Tosh was one of the three core members of the original Wailers, with Bob Marley and Bunny Wailer.
Peter Tosh's 1976 debut solo album was Legalize It.
Bunny Wailer was an original member of The Wailers and a three-time Grammy winner.
Toots and the Maytals' 1968 song "Do the Reggay" is credited with giving reggae its name.
Rolling Stone has named Toots Hibbert one of the 100 greatest singers.
Augustus Pablo played the melodica, which gave his dub and roots records a haunting, breathy sound.
King Tubby was a sound engineer whose experiments at the mixing desk helped invent dub.
Sugar Minott was a singer, producer and sound-system operator who gave many young artists their start.
All three members of Israel Vibration had polio as children, and they met at a rehabilitation centre.
Steel Pulse, from Handsworth in Birmingham, were the first non-Jamaican act to win the Grammy for Best Reggae Album.
Jimmy Cliff starred in the 1972 film The Harder They Come, which helped carry reggae around the world.
Desmond Dekker's "Israelites" in 1968 was one of the first international reggae hits.
Ken Boothe is known for his distinctive vibrato, and his song "Everything I Own" reached number one in the UK in 1974.
John Holt wrote "The Tide Is High" for The Paragons, years before Blondie made it a hit.
Drummer Sly Dunbar and bassist Robbie Shakespeare have played on hundreds of records by other artists.
U-Roy was a pioneer of toasting, talking rhythmically over records on a Jamaican sound system.
I-Roy, born Roy Reid, was one of the most prolific deejays of the 1970s.
Big Youth is a Jamaican deejay best known for his work in the 1970s.
Mikey Dread was a singer, producer and broadcaster.
Yellowman, born Winston Foster, became popular in Jamaica in the 1980s and is also known as King Yellowman.
Beres Hammond is known for his lovers rock music, and had his greatest success in the 1990s.
Sizzla has released more than fifty solo albums.
Capleton is also called King Shango, The Fireman and The Prophet.
Buju Banton, born Mark Myrie, is one of the most significant artists in Jamaican music.
Parov Stelar is Marcus Füreder, an Austrian producer considered a pioneer of electro swing.
Parov Stelar also makes visual art that has been shown in galleries.
Rüfüs Du Sol are a trio from Sydney: Tyrone Lindqvist, Jon George and James Hunt.
Röyksopp are a Norwegian duo from Tromsø, formed in 1998 by childhood friends Svein Berge and Torbjørn Brundtland.
Röyksopp's debut album Melody A.M. came out in 2001.
Nina Simone's stage presence earned her the title the High Priestess of Soul.
Nina Simone's piano playing was strongly shaped by Bach and classical music.
Paul Kalkbrenner breaks his tracks into pieces and rebuilds them on stage, so he is considered a live act rather than a DJ.
Paul Kalkbrenner's best-known track is "Sky and Sand".
Nina Kraviz is a Russian DJ, producer and singer.
Pet Shop Boys are Neil Tennant and Chris Lowe, formed in London in 1981, and they have sold more than 100 million records.
Orbital are the brothers Paul and Phil Hartnoll, and they took their name from London's M25 orbital motorway.
Chicane is the British producer Nick Bracegirdle, whose 1999 hit "Saltwater" sampled Enya.
Chromatics, from Portland, Oregon, were closely tied to Johnny Jewel's label Italians Do It Better.
Still Corners are a dream pop band formed in 2007 by songwriter Greg Hughes and singer Tessa Murray.
CamelPhat are Dave Whelan and Mike Di Scala, a duo from Liverpool who formed in 2006.
Oliver Koletzki is a Berlin DJ and producer who co-founded the label Stil vor Talent.
Oliver Koletzki broke through in 2005 with the track "Der Mückenschwarm".
Rhye is the project of Canadian singer Mike Milosh, and the first singles were released without any details about who was behind them.
The xx formed in Wandsworth, London in 2005, and their sound is built on a dual-vocalist set-up and a lot of space.
Radiohead formed in Abingdon, Oxfordshire in 1985.
Radiohead have worked with producer Nigel Godrich and cover artist Stanley Donwood since 1994.
Schiller is the project of the German musician Christopher von Deylen.
Nora En Pure is Daniela Di Lillo, a Swiss-South African deep house producer, who first got noticed with "Come With Me" in 2013.
Delerium began in 1987 as a side project of the industrial band Front Line Assembly.
Faithless formed in 1995 around Rollo, Sister Bliss and Maxi Jazz, and Rollo never performs live with the band.
Flight Facilities are Hugo Gruzman and James Lyell, who started by mixing other people's songs in 2009.
Flight Facilities also perform as Hugo & Jimmy.
Eli & Fur are Eliza Noble and Jennifer Skillman, a duo from London.
Roosevelt is a German singer, songwriter, DJ and producer.
Ross From Friends is Felix Weatherall, signed to the Brainfeeder label, and his debut album was Family Portrait in 2018.
Ane Brun is a Norwegian singer-songwriter of Sami origin who runs her own label, Balloon Ranger Recordings.
Oscar and the Wolf is the name used by the Belgian solo artist Max Colombie.
Cannons are an indie pop band from Los Angeles, formed in 2013.
Blank & Jones are a German duo who released their first single, "Sunrise", in 1997.
Kenneth Bager is a Danish musician and record producer.
Parra for Cuva is the German DJ Nicolas Demuth, best known for his house productions.
RY X is the Australian singer and producer Ry Cuming, the first artist signed to the Stockholm label Dumont Dumont.
Billie Eilish's sound leans on layered vocals and harmony lines built from double tracking.
Michael Jackson was known as the King of Pop, and his songs, videos and dancing changed how pop was made.
Rihanna comes from Barbados and has sold an estimated 250 million records.
Adele has won 16 Grammy Awards and 12 Brit Awards.
Black Coffee, born Nkosinathi Maphumulo, is a South African DJ who has won a Grammy for Best Dance/Electronic Album.
Salif Keïta, called the Golden Voice of Africa, comes from Mali's royal Keita family.
Lana Del Rey's songs are known for a melancholy take on romance and glamour, full of 1950s to 1970s Americana.
Tems, from Nigeria, rose to prominence after singing on Wizkid's 2020 single "Essence".
Libianca is a Cameroonian singer whose breakout single was "People" in 2022, after she appeared on The Voice in 2021.
Dennis Ferrer is a New York soulful house producer who founded the Objektivity label.
London Grammar's debut album If You Wait reached number 2 on the UK albums chart in 2013.
Dua Lipa has won seven Brit Awards and three Grammys.
The Black Eyed Peas formed in Los Angeles in 1992 and have sold an estimated 80 million records.
Tyla, from South Africa, is nicknamed the Queen of Popiano for blending pop with amapiano.
Beyoncé is widely regarded as one of the greatest entertainers of all time.
Kygo is a Norwegian DJ who helped bring tropical house to the mainstream, starting with his 2013 remix of "I See Fire".
Technotronic's "Pump Up the Jam" reached number 2 in the US in 1989.
Everything but the Girl are Tracey Thorn and Ben Watt, formed in Hull in 1982.
Sade was made an Officer of the Order of the British Empire in 2002.
The Weeknd, born Abel Tesfaye, is known for his falsetto and the cinematic videos that go with his songs.
Empire of the Sun are Luke Steele and Nick Littlemore, an Australian duo formed in 2007.
Kenya Grace's 2023 single "Strangers" reached number one on the UK singles chart.
Robert Miles was the Italian producer whose 1995 instrumental "Children" topped charts around the world.
Euphonik, born Themba Nkosi, is a South African DJ and producer, known mostly for house music.
Black Motion are an Afro house duo from Soshanguve, South Africa, formed in 2010.
Dlala Thukzin comes from Lamontville, KwaZulu-Natal, and blends amapiano, afro tech and gqom.
Musa Keys' 2021 single "Vula Mlomo" went double platinum in South Africa.
Clean Bandit formed in Cambridge in 2008 and have had four UK number-one singles.
P!nk is known for performing acrobatics on stage.
John Summit is a tech house DJ who used to be an accountant, and he runs the label Experts Only.
Zerb is a Brazilian DJ best known for his 2023 hit "Mwaki".
DJ Maphorisa has produced for artists including Wizkid, Drake and Black Coffee.
Kabza De Small is a major figure in amapiano, and a member of the Scorpion Kings.
Black Sheep are Dres and Mista Lawnge, and they were part of the Native Tongues collective with De La Soul and A Tribe Called Quest.
Dres and Mista Lawnge of Black Sheep met as teenagers in North Carolina.
Terminator X was the DJ for Public Enemy until he left in 1998.
The Whooliganz were a 1990s hip hop duo made up of Scott Caan and Alan Maman, who rapped as Mad Skillz and Mudfoot.
A Lighter Shade of Brown, from Riverside, California, are best known for their 1990 single "On a Sunday Afternoon".
Sunz of Man is a Wu-Tang Clan affiliated group from New York.
